title: Mind Over Mood: Change How You Feel By Changing the Way You Think
author: Dennis Greenberger and Christine A. Padesky
edition_analyzed: Second Edition (2015), widely used in clinical and self-help settings
target_audience: Individuals experiencing depression, anxiety, anger, or other mood disorders
People interested in learning CBT techniques for emotional well-being
Students and educators in psychology or counseling
General readers seeking tools to manage their emotions
core_themes: The connection between thoughts, feelings, and behaviors
Empowering individuals to manage mood through cognitive change
Practical skills for identifying and challenging negative thinking patterns
Building resilience and long-term emotional health
primary_purpose: To teach readers, through hands-on exercises and guided worksheets, how to apply cognitive behavioral therapy principles to understand and improve their moods, break patterns of negative thinking, and cope with emotional difficulties more effectively.

structure_format.organization: Organized into progressive chapters building CBT skills step-by-step; includes worksheets, real-life case examples, summaries, and practice assignments

key_concepts_lessons: Moods are influenced by our thinking, and changing thoughts can change emotional states.
Automatic thoughts can be identified, recorded, and evaluated for accuracy.
Cognitive distortions (like all-or-nothing thinking and catastrophizing) contribute to negative emotions and can be challenged.
Behavioral experiments and activity scheduling can help break cycles of depression and avoidance.
CBT tools are practical, learnable, and can be used independently or with professional support.
Self-compassion and persistence are crucial in the change process.
notable_features: Accessible language designed for laypeople and professionals
Widely used in individual and group therapy as well as self-guided use
Step-by-step, modular structure suited for gradual learning
cultural_historical_context: Originally published as CBT was gaining prominence as an effective treatment for mood disorders, 'Mind Over Mood' became a seminal guide both for therapists and the general public. The second edition updates examples and includes expanded resources for diverse cultures and conditions.
reception_impact: International bestseller and a standard CBT workbook
Recommended by mental health professionals and used in thousands of clinics worldwide
Praised for clear structure, user-friendly exercises, and adaptability to a range of problems
Recipient of the Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies Book of Merit
Some readers find the worksheet-intensive approach repetitive or clinical without guidance
comparable_titles: Feeling Good: The New Mood Therapy by David D. Burns
The Anxiety and Phobia Workbook by Edmund J. Bourne
The Cognitive Behavioral Workbook for Depression by William J. Knaus
The Happiness Trap by Russ Harris
